text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Final non-aligned movement declaration calls on member countries to freeze ties with Israel.
- Egypt calls on Israel to halt settlements in East Jerusalem.
- European Union proposes joint Middle East initiative with U.S.
- Hebron witnesses strong protests against Israeli forces; three Palestinians martyred and more than 100 wounded.
- Oman stresses commitment to Arab League decisions to freeze ties with Israel.
- Protesters in U.S. condemn Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu.
- Arabs meet in Cairo to coordinate policies on security and political issues to be discussed next week at Euro-Mediterranean meeting.
- Syrian Defence Minister Tlas meets Japanese military delegation visiting Syria to inspect Japanese U.N. unit operating on Golan Heights.
- U.S. company studies possibility of establishing plant to dry vegetables that would be exported to U.S.
- Pakistan says it won't establish ties with Israel as long as Jewish state still occupies Arab lands.
- Moslem Eid pilgrimage to start on April 17.
- Syrian cabinet discusses agricultural situation, crops, water storage.
- Israelis try to buy land in Jordan.
